evidence.quote: persons that conduct business in this state or persons that produce products or services that are targeted to residents of this state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Connecticut's Public Act 22-15 gives state residents rights over their personal data, including opt-out rights for targeted advertising, data sales and certain profiling. It imposes controller and processor duties on businesses above volume thresholds, effective 1 July 2023, enforced exclusively by the Attorney General.
summary.long: Public Act 22-15 (SB 6) applies to persons that conduct business in Connecticut or target products or services to its residents and that, in the preceding calendar year, controlled or processed personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, or of at least 25,000 consumers while deriving more than 25 per cent of gross revenue from selling personal data. It exempts state bodies, nonprofits, higher-education institutions, Gramm-Leach-Bliley financial institutions, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, and listed categories of data. Consumers may confirm, access, correct, delete and port their personal data, and opt out of targeted advertising, data sales and certain solely automated profiling. Controllers must limit collection, secure data, obtain consent for sensitive data, avoid unlawful discrimination, provide a privacy notice, and from 1 January 2025 honour opt-out preference signals. Processors must follow controller instructions under a binding contract. Controllers must conduct data protection assessments for targeted advertising, data sales, certain profiling and sensitive data processing. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority; from 1 July 2023 to 31 December 2024 it must issue notice and allow a sixty-day cure period, and the Act creates no private right of action. A task force is convened to study related topics and report.

notes: Text is Public Act 22-15 as approved May 10, 2022; no consolidated version was supplied. Sections 1 to 12 are new law (marked NEW), so no other statute is amended or repealed. Cross-reference rows list the main federal and Connecticut citations, not every citation in the text. target_instrument_id is empty because no registry IDs were supplied. Internal points: the Sec. 11(b) cure period runs from July 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024 and the Sec. 11(c) cure factors apply from January 1, 2025. Sec. 12(d) requires the task force report 'not later than January 1, 2023', while the task force terminates on the report date 'or January 1, 2023, whichever is later'. Sec. 12 is effective from passage; other sections from July 1, 2023. Bill page headers recur throughout the text.
